setups.name: AGENTS.md Baseline
setups.description: One fill-in-the-blanks instruction file shared by several agents, plus a one-line CLAUDE.md that imports it, so your project rules stop drifting between tools.
setups.readme:
# AGENTS.md Baseline

One instruction file that several coding agents can share, instead of a separate copy per
tool that slowly drifts apart.

## What is inside

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | A fill-in-the-blanks template: project summary, commands, layout, conventions, boundaries, definition of done. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | A one-line file that imports `AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code reads the same instructions. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT. |

## Install

1. Copy `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` into the root of your repository.
2. Open `AGENTS.md` and replace every line in `<angle brackets>` with facts about your
   project. Delete sections you do not need.
3. Commit both files.

If you already have a `CLAUDE.md`, do not overwrite it. Add the line `@AGENTS.md` at the top
of your existing file instead.

## Compatibility

Declared by the author, not independently tested by Kitloom:

- **Codex** reads `AGENTS.md` from the repository root.
- **Cursor** reads `AGENTS.md` from the repository root.
- **Claude Code** reads `CLAUDE.md`, which imports `AGENTS.md` through the `@` import syntax.

Agent behaviour changes between versions. Check your agent's documentation if the file does
not seem to be picked up.

## Customising

Shorter is better. Agents load this file every session, so each line costs context. Keep
commands exact, keep rules specific to this project, and move long reference material into
separate documents that you link to.

## Safety

This kit contains Markdown only. It does not include scripts, hooks, or tool configuration.

setups.name: Review Pass
setups.description: A repeatable code-review procedure: an editable checklist, a fixed severity-ranked report format, and a report-only rule. Ships as a Claude Code slash command and a Cursor rule.
setups.readme:
# Review Pass

A repeatable code-review procedure for coding agents: one editable checklist, one fixed
report format, and a rule that the agent only reports and never edits.

## What is inside

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.claude/commands/review.md` | Claude Code slash command `/review [base]`. |
| `.cursor/rules/review.mdc` | Cursor rule the agent applies when you ask for a review. |
| `docs/review-checklist.md` | The checklist both of them read. Edit this to fit your project. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT. |

## Install

1. Copy `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, and `docs/review-checklist.md` into your repository root,
   merging with any folders that already exist. You can skip the folder for an agent you
   do not use.
2. Edit `docs/review-checklist.md`. Remove what does not apply and add your own rules.
3. Commit the files.

If you move the checklist, update the path inside both the command and the rule.

## Use

- **Claude Code:** run `/review` to compare against `main`, or `/review develop` to compare
  against another branch or commit.
- **Cursor:** ask the agent to review your changes. The rule is attached when relevant
  because of its description; it is not always on.

Findings come back most severe first:

```
[blocker] src/billing/invoice.ts:88 — total is computed before discounts are applied
  Why: an order with a 100% coupon is charged the full amount
  Fix: move applyDiscounts() above the total calculation
```

## Compatibility

Declared by the author, not independently tested by Kitloom: Claude Code (custom slash
commands in `.claude/commands/`) and Cursor (project rules in `.cursor/rules/`).

## Safety

Markdown only. The Claude Code command asks the agent to run `git diff` and `git status`,
which read your repository and change nothing. It contains no hooks and no scripts.

setups.name: Debug Loop
setups.description: A Claude Code skill for systematic debugging: reproduce first, narrow the gap, test one hypothesis at a time, and prove the fix with a failing-then-passing test. Includes a git bisect reference.
setups.readme:
# Debug Loop

A Claude Code skill that makes the agent debug the slow, correct way: reproduce the failure,
narrow it down, test one hypothesis at a time, and prove the fix with a test that fails
first.

## What is inside

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/debug-loop/SKILL.md` | The five-step procedure and the conditions for stopping to ask. |
| `.claude/skills/debug-loop/references/bisecting.md` | How to find the commit that introduced a regression with `git bisect`. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT. |

## Install

Copy the `.claude/skills/debug-loop/` folder into your repository so the path is
`.claude/skills/debug-loop/SKILL.md`. To make it available in every project instead, copy
it to `~/.claude/skills/debug-loop/`.

## Use

Claude Code loads the skill on its own when a task matches the description: a failing test,
a bug report, or unexplained behaviour. You can also ask for it by name, for example
"use the debug-loop skill on this failing test".

## Compatibility

Declared by the author for Claude Code (project skills in `.claude/skills/`). Not
independently tested by Kitloom. The procedure in `SKILL.md` is plain Markdown, so you can
paste it into another agent's instruction file, but that use is not declared here.

## Customising

Edit the stop conditions at the bottom of `SKILL.md` to match how much autonomy you want
the agent to have. Add your project's test and debugger commands to step 1.

## Safety

Markdown only. The reference file describes `git bisect`, which checks out other commits in
your working tree; the skill tells the agent to commit or stash first. There are no hooks
and no scripts.

setups.name: Docs Voice
setups.description: Documentation rules that make agents verify claims against the code, write for the reader, and keep READMEs, guides, and changelogs consistent. A Claude Code skill and a matching Cursor rule.
setups.readme:
# Docs Voice

Documentation rules for coding agents, so generated READMEs and guides are verified against
the code, written for the reader, and consistent from one page to the next.

## What is inside

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/write-docs/SKILL.md` | Claude Code skill: what to check before writing, style, structure, changelogs. |
| `.cursor/rules/docs.mdc` | Cursor rule with the same guidance, attached to `*.md` and `*.mdx` files. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT. |

## Install

Copy the folder for the agent you use into your repository root, merging with existing
folders:

- Claude Code: `.claude/skills/write-docs/`
- Cursor: `.cursor/rules/docs.mdc`

## Use

- **Claude Code** loads the skill when you ask it to document something or update a README.
- **Cursor** attaches the rule when the agent works on a Markdown file matched by the
  `globs` pattern.

## Compatibility

Declared by the author, not independently tested by Kitloom: Claude Code (project skills in
`.claude/skills/`) and Cursor (project rules in `.cursor/rules/`).

## Customising

Both files carry the same rules in two formats. If you change one, change the other. Add
your project's terminology, the tone you want, and any house rules for headings or
capitalisation.

## Safety

Markdown only. No scripts, hooks, or tool configuration.
